source.title: Do Vision and Language Encoders Represent the World Similarly?
source.authors: Mayug Maniparambil; Raiymbek Akshulakov; Y. Djilali; Sanath Narayan; Mohamed El Amine Seddik; K. Mangalam; Noel E. O'Connor

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Measures cross-modal representational similarity with CKA and evaluates whether that similarity supports matching and retrieval. This is a conceptual test of representation alignment, not the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on vision-language CKA, dataset/model comparisons, shuffle sensitivity, and cross-modal retrieval. Those are recorded below. Results cited from prior work, ImageNet classification results, and method runtime comparisons are omitted because they do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-modal CKA and training-free matching between independently trained vision and text encoders across training data, paradigm, model and layer. These are its own results on V1, V2, V4, V6 and V7, using different methods from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that vision encoders trained on sufficiently large datasets show high semantic similarity to language encoders, comparable to aligned encoders, irrespective of training paradigm. They exploit this via QAP matching and local CKA for zero-shot matching and retrieval, outperforming relative representations. Training-data scale, curation and language supervision raise alignment.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CKA and cross-modal image-caption matching/retrieval rather than testing the original Platonic claim's broad alignment trend with its original procedure. It does not replicate the original Convergent Learning seed-based setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment varies with shuffling of pair order, choice of encoder and layer, language, text encoder, vision training paradigm, and training-data size and curation.
record.problems: The scale trend is described from plotted comparisons without exact values in the main-text description. Experiments largely hold the text encoder fixed, do not directly measure capability, and do not isolate whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment. Results averaged over three seeds are reported without dispersion statistics.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant reported results were left out within the 60-row limit. CKA values from the cross-lingual paired-model table are not separately catalogued because the table layout does not clearly assign its two CKA columns to each language/model pairing.

untested.parts: Vision model size scaling and joint scaling of both models. Convergence across many architectures and objectives within one modality. A direct capability measure.
Joint improvement of both encoders. Text side tested only via model size and language-specific versus multilingual encoders.
Stitching layers and mapping without paired data. Linear regression appears only as a baseline.
All: no feature or circuit analysis.
Broad set of similarity metrics and number-of-neighbours settings.
Plateau. Shared training data as the cause.

missing.what: Metric ablation: normalized correlation matrix gives 10.1% QAP matching versus 48.8% with CKA. Stretching and clustering raise matching to 65.5%.
Kernel CKA of CLIP's own text encoder versus a multilingual encoder across 11 languages (e.g. ko 0.154 versus 0.620). The table layout is readable: CLIP column and Ours column.
Vision objective effect: classification ViT 35.3 QAP versus DETR 26.5, DPT 22.7, SegFormer 16.8
Text model size has limited impact on CKA
Layerwise QAP values (CLIP 0.29 to 0.79 at projection; DINOv2+Roberta rising to 0.672)
Linear regression mapping baseline (e.g. DINOv2 COCO top-5 65.4, matching 45.1) and 2-layer MLP projection (59.8 QAP-acc equivalent)
Matching accuracy depends on number of anchors and queries

record.verdict_notes: Main fixes: r12 subject is the CLIP ViT-L/14-336 vision encoder, not DINOv2-large. V6 links were removed from model-pair CKA rows and from the shuffle control rows (r1-r6), which are pairing sanity checks. Table A.13 rows lack baselines, so the data-scale trend is readable only across rows. Several claim-relevant tables (6, 4 CKA columns, A.8, A.3/A.4) are unrecorded.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish a general rise in alignment as models become more capable, or jointly scale independently trained models across architectures, objectives, data, and modalities. The reported comparisons are primarily vision encoders against a selected text encoder.
Does not sweep the capability of both encoders together or establish a general trend as both improve. Most experiments use fixed image-caption datasets and selected encoders.
No comparison of independently initialized seeds of the same architecture or shared feature subspaces.
Tests zero-shot cross-modal matching and retrieval, not linear maps, layer stitching, or mapping without paired data.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Tests input ordering, CKA versus a correlation-matrix alternative, model/layer choices, and some dataset/language settings; does not systematically compare a broad set of similarity metrics or out-of-distribution inputs.

Compares training paradigms and data regimes but does not isolate shared training data/objectives as the cause of alignment, measure a plateau, or determine whether a common model of reality explains the similarity.
